author: sky.cactus
content: I can definitely see regret in moving to 10s.  One can imagine a future where 10s vs 12s is negligible in terms of user experience and performance so the benefits are, overall, negligible.  We never reduce the slot time more than that for whatever reason(s).  However we end up having to deal with a bunch of problems caused by tooling built on top of Ethereum that assumed 12 seconds having weird bugs and bizarre behaviors.  Apps that were built and passed the walk away test (and developers walked away) don't work quite right anymore, and while none of them totally break they suffer from weird edge case things that are confusing to the user or result in a worse user experience.  So we end up getting negligible benefit and ecosystem wide frustration and overall reduced UX.

author: barnabemonnot
content: We started surveying apps (see here https://x.com/SourcifyEth/status/2086740760008012030) and poll some infras informally for now. Do you know example of apps that could break?

author: sky.cactus
content: The Interceptor (a browser extension that passes the walk away test) hard-codes block time because the RPC server doesn't provide a way to query for block time, and we didn't want to add a bunch of complexity to estimate block time by watching historical blocks for a feature that may never be needed.  Estimating blocks would have a bunch of edge cases, like along fork boundaries and when a slot is missed, that would need to be handled to do it correctly.
